newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse taken higher by high-caps.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse taken higher by high-caps.

text.p: High volumes traded in Bucharest bourse first-tier Oltchim and Azomures and special deals in the two high-caps on Tuesday hoisted turnover to 2.1 billion lei from 1.5 billion.
Chemical plant Oltchim SA and Azomures SA fertiliser maker took a combined 96 percent of turnover and both closed stronger on the previous session.

Oltchim had a turnover of 1.1 billion lei, with some 165 million from a special trade, and closed 150 lei stronger at 1,650. Special trades are deals worth more than 100 million lei struck outside the market and reported to the exchange later.
Two special deals worth some 396 million lei in Azomures took its turnover to around 874 million and helped it close 70 lei higher at 1,600.
Buying interest in the other stocks was thin, with most shares drifting lower or staying flat and three stocks having no trade.
Brokers said an appreciated leu currency, as well as high interest rates on banking deposits stripped the bourse of some of its attraction.
"Investors who flocked to the market a few weeks ago are now starting to place their money elsewhere," said a broker.
Traders said they expected foreign demand also to grow thinner in the sessions to come due to the firmer leu.
"Unless the dollar puts on some weight in the weeks ahead there will also be fewer foreign investors on the market," a trader said.
Two unofficial indices -- the VAB and the BIG -- fell from the previous session by 9.2 and respectively 7.24 percent.
The two brokerage houses explained the fall in their computed indices, saying it reflected lower average prices for hich-caps Azomures and Oltchim.
